landing.faq.title: Online Manim AI generator: frequently asked questions.
landing.faq.description: Direct answers about Manim Community support, local setup, code editing, rendering, and CurvG's current availability.
landing.faq.stack.question: What's the tech stack?
landing.faq.stack.answer: Next.js 16 with the App Router, React 19, TypeScript strict mode, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn/ui, Drizzle ORM, and better-auth. Every piece of business logic is inlined — no external packages for payment, email, storage, or AI.
landing.faq.payment.question: Which payment providers are supported?
landing.faq.payment.answer: Stripe, PayPal, Creem, Alipay, and WeChat Pay out of the box. The PaymentManager abstraction makes it straightforward to add more providers by implementing a single interface.
landing.faq.database.question: Which databases can I use?
landing.faq.database.answer: Drizzle ORM handles PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Turso, and Cloudflare D1. Switch providers by editing DATABASE_PROVIDER in your .env — the schema templates and drizzle config adapt automatically.
landing.faq.customize.question: How customizable is the landing page?
landing.faq.customize.answer: The src/blocks/ directory ships with demo sections — they're designed to be rewritten per project. The durable primitives live in src/components/, so your rebrand touches blocks and translations, not the chassis.
landing.faq.license.question: Can I use this for commercial projects?
landing.faq.license.answer: Yes. ShipAny Next is built for shipping production SaaS products. You own the code after cloning — no per-seat fees, no runtime dependencies on our infrastructure.

landing.workflow.eyebrow: How the Manim AI generator works
landing.workflow.title: Create visual math animations in three reviewable steps.
landing.workflow.description: CurvG separates prompt interpretation, scene planning, code generation, and rendering so errors can be found before they become an exported video.
landing.workflow.describe.title: Write a text prompt
landing.workflow.describe.description: Describe a formula, mathematical concept, or teaching objective. Include the objects, labels, transformations, and timing that matter.
landing.workflow.direct.title: Review the plan and generated code
landing.workflow.direct.description: Inspect assumptions, formulas, storyboard order, axes, labels, camera framing, and timing before submitting Manim Community code.
landing.workflow.render.title: Render when the environment is ready
landing.workflow.render.description: An approved scene can be sent to the isolated renderer when it is configured. Until then, the generated Python remains available to inspect and copy.
landing.workflow.status_text: Confirm the equation and explanation sequence before code and rendering. Problems surface earlier, and you can revise only the part that needs attention.
landing.faq.what_is.question: What is CurvG AI, and how does it use Manim?
landing.faq.what_is.answer: Manim is a Python engine for precise mathematical animation and is closely associated with the visual explanations popularized by 3Blue1Brown. CurvG AI is an independent Manim AI generator that turns text prompts into a structured scene specification and Manim Community Python code, with a review step before rendering.
landing.faq.version.question: Which version of Manim does CurvG AI target?
landing.faq.version.answer: The isolated renderer image currently pins Manim Community 0.20.1. Generated code uses the Community Edition import and a constrained CurvGScene class so the output can be validated against the renderer's execution rules.
landing.faq.installation.question: Do I need Python, FFmpeg, or LaTeX installed locally?
landing.faq.installation.answer: Not for prompt planning or Manim code generation in the web workspace. Video execution still depends on a configured isolated renderer; CurvG does not currently present public remote rendering as production-ready.
landing.faq.editing.question: Can I edit and compile the generated Manim code in the browser?
landing.faq.editing.answer: Not yet. The current Creator lets you inspect and copy generated Python, but it is not a full online Manim editor or general-purpose online Manim compiler. Direct in-browser code editing has not been implemented.
landing.faq.free.question: Can I use CurvG AI for free?
landing.faq.free.answer: CurvG has not published paid plans or a permanent free tier with daily compilation credits. The current build is early access; pricing and usage limits will be published only after production rendering costs and reliability are measured.
landing.faq.difference.question: How is CurvG different from a one-click AI video generator?
landing.faq.difference.answer: A one-click generator can hide formula mistakes and scene logic inside a prompt-to-video black box. CurvG exposes formulas, assumptions, storyboard steps, and Manim code before rendering. It does not claim that AI output is automatically mathematically correct.
landing.faq.accuracy.question: Can AI guarantee a mathematically correct animation?
landing.faq.accuracy.answer: No. A model can misread notation, make a false assumption, or generate incorrect scene logic. CurvG keeps formulas, assumptions, specifications, code, and previews visible so a person can find errors before export; it does not replace mathematical review.
landing.faq.rendering.question: Is remote Manim rendering live in production?
landing.faq.rendering.answer: Not yet. The local Queue-to-Sandbox-to-Manim-to-R2 path has rendered a real MP4 and thumbnail, but production Cloudflare resources and a complete real-model request have not been tested. CurvG therefore does not present public remote rendering as production-ready.
landing.faq.use_cases.question: What kinds of math animations can CurvG help plan?
landing.faq.use_cases.answer: The workflow is designed for parametric and polar curves, graph transformations, visual proofs, calculus explanations, Fourier and wave demonstrations, and physics scenes. Each project still requires the user to review the mathematics and visual sequence.
landing.faq.formats.question: Which export formats are planned?
landing.faq.formats.answer: The initial target is downloadable Manim source plus MP4 preview and final video files. WebM and GIF should only be added after real demand and conversion-cost testing.
landing.faq.availability.question: What can I use in the current build?
landing.faq.availability.answer: Formula-driven previews, the Creator review flow, specification approval, Manim code generation, and the local isolated renderer path are implemented. Real-model end-to-end testing, production Cloudflare validation, and public gallery publishing are still pending.
landing.faq.cloudflare.question: Why use a Cloudflare-native architecture?
landing.faq.cloudflare.answer: CurvG uses Workers for API orchestration, D1 for product metadata, R2 for render artifacts, and Cloudflare Sandbox for isolated code execution. The local path is verified, but production runtime limits, concurrency, permissions, and cost still need workload testing.
landing.pricing.meta_title: CurvG Pricing & Early Access | Manim Animation Generator
landing.pricing.meta_description: CurvG has not published paid plans. Join early access while production Manim rendering, Cloudflare limits, storage, and model costs are measured.
landing.pricing.factor_render_descriptio: Scene duration, output resolution, LaTeX use, geometry complexity, and container startup all affect the cost of a Manim render.
landing.pricing.factor_capacity_descript: Plans must account for queue delay, parallel jobs, timeouts, retries, and failed renders instead of assuming every request succeeds first time.
landing.pricing.factor_storage_descripti: Source code, logs, thumbnails, previews, final videos, downloads, and retention periods create separate R2 storage and delivery costs.
landing.pricing.note: CurvG will not advertise lifetime, unlimited, or fixed-credit plans until representative production workloads make those limits defensible.
landing.footer.disclaimer: Manim is an open-source project maintained by the Manim Community. CurvG AI is an independent product and is not affiliated with the Manim Community or 3Blue1Brown.

landing.why.description: CurvG combines text-to-Manim planning, structured review, and constrained Manim Community code generation. The workflow exposes what the model understood before code reaches a renderer.
landing.why.clarity.title: Text-to-Manim generation
landing.why.clarity.item_1_description: Convert a mathematical request into explicit assumptions, formulas, visual objects, actions, camera rules, and timing.
landing.why.clarity.item_2_description: Generate one self-contained CurvGScene using constrained Manim APIs and standard Python language features.
landing.why.clarity.item_3_description: If generated JSON or code fails structural validation, the model receives the validation reason and produces a corrected response.
landing.why.control.title: Review before execution
landing.why.control.item_1_description: Review formulas, assumptions, scene order, labels, framing, and duration before approving code generation.
landing.why.control.item_2_description: Keep the Python visible and portable. The current workspace supports inspection and copying; direct browser editing is not yet implemented.
landing.why.control.item_3_description: When configured, approved code is submitted to a separate renderer instead of executing inside the web application process.
